autopsy.headline: The egress guard is winning the same battle on repeat — scrubbing restart-banner scaffold text out of Discord messages dozens of times — because the harness injects its own '[System: Bot just restarted]' banners into the agent's context and nothing upstream stops the agent from parroting them back out, including one case where the entire outbound message was scaffold and was sanitized to an empty string.

annotations.annotation: Identical FM-005 events ('[System: Bot just restarted]' embedded mid-sentence in 'ok here's the update...') recur at least 4 times verbatim. The guard fires deterministically every time, but recurrence at this frequency means the violation is being sanitized, not corrected — the agent never receives a signal that it echoed scaffold text, so it keeps doing it.

'Bot just restarted: previous task was AWG email draft' shows the agent leaking cross-session task state (the AWG email draft) into a public channel. This isn't just cosmetic banner echo — restart banners carry prior-task metadata, so FM-005 here doubles as an information-disclosure vector.

The '[Channel: #shadow-hq] [System: Bot just restarted. Completed before restart: nothing]' events sanitize to an empty string — the agent's entire intended message was scaffold. The guard 'passes' by sending nothing, which silently drops a turn. Sanitization has no floor: an empty-after-sanitize result should be a block-and-regenerate, not a send.

These events are tagged FM-005 (context-miss: 'asking Will to repeat something'), but the observed behavior is scaffold-token egress, which matches no taxonomy entry. The taxonomy has a hole and the closest label was borrowed — meaning frequency stats for the real failure mode are being miscounted under an unrelated one.

Consistent inverse correlation: when fetch_tools is empty (no browse_url call), hedge=true; when a fetch actually ran, hedge=false. The carveout is correctly downgrading unfetched home_diy/health_nutrition advice to hedged language — this contract is working as designed and provides the counterexample to the egress guard's Sisyphean loop.

The only hard block in the window: externally checkable text shipped with no claim manifest. Unlike the egress guard's sanitize-and-forward posture, this gate refuses outright — and notably, it does not recur, suggesting block-severity contracts extinguish the behavior while sanitize-severity contracts merely mask it.

root_cause_chain: Surface symptom: Discord messages in #shadow-hq repeatedly contain restart banners like '[System: Bot just restarted]' and '[Channel: #shadow-hq]', caught and stripped by the egress guard.

The agent treats these banners as message content because the harness injects them inline into the same context stream as real conversation, with no structural marker distinguishing scaffold from user-visible text.
The egress guard operates sanitize-only at the sink: it cleans the output but returns no error to the agent, so the generating behavior is never penalized and repeats verbatim across restarts.
Because restarts happen frequently and each restart re-injects the banner, every post-restart turn re-triggers the same leak — the failure rate is coupled to restart frequency, not to agent learning.

Structural cause: contamination is handled at egress instead of ingress. Scaffold metadata enters the model's context unquarantined, guaranteeing the model will sometimes reproduce it; no contract exists for the actual failure mode, so it was shoehorned into FM-005 and never triaged as its own problem.

missing_contract.name: scaffold-context-quarantine
missing_contract.trigger: Any harness-generated banner or metadata line (restart notices, channel tags, prior-task summaries) being appended to the agent-visible context, and any egress payload that sanitizes to empty.
missing_contract.precondition: Scaffold text must be injected only inside a structurally tagged, non-echoable envelope (or stripped before model ingestion); an egress message whose sanitized form is empty must block and force regeneration rather than send.
missing_contract.why_it_would_have_caught_this: Every FM-005 event in this window originates from the same injected restart banner. Quarantining it at ingress removes the source, so the egress guard never fires; the empty-after-sanitize rule catches the degenerate case where the agent's whole message was scaffold, converting a silent dropped turn into a visible, correctable failure. It also stops prior-task metadata ('AWG email draft') from ever being candidate output to a public channel.

autopsy.buyer_takeaway: This trace shows deterministic enforcement doing exactly what prompt-only guardrails cannot: the egress guard caught 100% of scaffold leaks including a cross-session task disclosure, and the entailment gate hard-blocked an unmanifested claim — no amount of 'don't echo system text' prompting achieves that reliability. But it also shows the limit of enforcement without feedback: a sanitize-only contract fires forever because the agent never learns, while the one block-severity contract in the window fired exactly once. The lesson for buyers is that contracts must close the loop — quarantine at ingress, block rather than silently clean at egress — or you buy perfect detection of a failure you never fix.
